## Why This Is Asked
Tests secret mounting, env wiring, and health checks for TLS in a CKAD context.

## Key Concepts
- Secret as files
- Env vars from paths
- Readiness checks for TLS paths
- Rollout validation and rollback criteria

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payments
  namespace: prod
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: payments
        image: your-image
        env:
        - name: TLS_CERT_FILE
          value: /tls/tls.crt
        - name: TLS_KEY_FILE
          value: /tls/tls.key
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls-volume
          mountPath: /tls
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
      volumes:
      - name: tls-volume
        secret:
          secretName: tls-secret
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate zero-downtime during rollout with TLS cert changes?
- How would you audit access to tls-secret in Pod logs?

## Why This Is Asked
Explores practical CKAD competencies: deployment orchestration, config/secret management, volumes, autoscaling, service exposure, and network isolation.

## Key Concepts
- Deployment, PVC, ConfigMap/Secret, HPA
- ClusterIP service semantics
- NetworkPolicy gating and its limitations

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-app
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: my-app:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: my-app-config
        - secretRef:
            name: my-app-creds
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: data-pvc
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: data-pvc
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
  storageClassName: standard
---
apiVersion: autoscaling/v1
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: my-app-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: my-app
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 10
  targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 60
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: my-app
spec:
  selector:
    app: my-app
  ports:
  - port: 8080
    targetPort: 8080
  type: ClusterIP
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-egress-api
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 203.0.113.0/24
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test this in a cluster with a restricted CNI?
- What changes if the app becomes stateful or requires dynamic PVC provisioning?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical hardening: container securityContext, readiness/liveness, graceful shutdown, high-availability with PDB, and network isolation via NetworkPolicy.

## Key Concepts
- Pod securityContext and container securityContext
- Probes and lifecycle hooks
- PodDisruptionBudget
- NetworkPolicy basics and egress constraints
- Per-namespace isolation in production-grade CKAD

## Code Example
```javascript
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api
  namespace: secure
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: api:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsUser: 10001
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config
          mountPath: /etc/api-config
        - name: secret
          mountPath: /etc/api-secret
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "512Mi"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /readyz
            port: 8080
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 5"]
      volumes:
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: api-config
      - name: secret
        secret:
          secretName: api-secret
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: api-pdb
  namespace: secure
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: api-egress
  namespace: secure
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
      ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.96.0.0/12
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:
      namespaceSelector: {}
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you monitor and validate performance under load?
- How would you rollback the namespace isolation changes safely?

## Why This Is Asked
This tests practical CKAD pattern: file-driven config synchronization, idempotent object creation, secret management, and namespace-scoped network policy.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer tooling, kubectl in-cluster, ConfigMap/Secret management, TLS sidecar, NetworkPolicy scoping.
- Cadence-based reconciliation and minimal YAML skeletons for CKAD.

## Code Example
```javascript
# Minimal skeleton for a Deployment that performs config sync
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: config-sync
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: config-sync
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: alpine:3.17
          command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache jq curl kubectl"]
      containers:
        - name: main
          image: my-registry/config-sync:latest
          env:
            - name: SYNC_INTERVAL
              value: "300s"
      volumes:
        - name: config
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: config-pvc
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /health
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 10
        periodSeconds: 5
      livenessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /health
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 30
        periodSeconds: 10
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you secure the TLS sidecar and rotate certs without restarting pods?
- How would you test reconciliation and conflict resolution between file changes and cluster objects?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests knowledge of namespace-scoped governance primitives (LimitRange, ResourceQuota) and how defaults affect scheduling, QoS, and multi-tenant fairness in CKAD.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace scoping
- LimitRange defaultRequests/defaultLimits
- ResourceQuota hard limits
- Pod scheduling under quotas
- Impact on autoscaling and experimentation

## Code Example
```yaml
# Namespace
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: test-ns
---
# LimitRange
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: default-limits
  namespace: test-ns
spec:
  limits:
  - default:
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 256Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    type: Container
---
# ResourceQuota
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: resource-quota
  namespace: test-ns
spec:
  hard:
    pods: "10"
    requests.cpu: "1"
    requests.memory: 1Gi
    limits.cpu: "2"
    limits.memory: 2Gi
---
# Deployment (inherits defaults)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: sample-app
  namespace: test-ns
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: sample-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: sample-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
```

## Trade-offs
**Advantages:**
- Prevents resource starvation across namespaces
- Enforces fair resource distribution
- Automatic defaults reduce configuration errors
- Provides cost control boundaries

**Considerations:**
- Too restrictive limits can hinder scaling
- Default limits may be overprovisioned for small workloads
- ResourceQuota refusals require manual quota increases
- May impact autoscaling behavior if quotas are too tight

**Best Practices:**
- Set conservative defaults but allow overrides
- Monitor quota utilization regularly
- Use separate quotas for production vs development
- Consider pod priority classes for critical workloads

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a maintenance task that runs in Kubernetes using CronJob, PVCs, and ConfigMaps. It also covers secrets, sidecars, probes, and egress constraints in a realistic operational scenario.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes CronJob, PersistentVolumeClaim, ConfigMap, Secret

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: log-cleaner
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  schedule: '0 * * * *'
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: cleaner
            image: registry.example.com/log-cleaner:latest
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs

            envFrom:
            - configMapRef:

          initContainers:

            command: ['sh', '-c', 'apk add --no-cache gzip pigz curl']
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

- How would you rollback a CronJob update and validate it touched no data loss?

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:

spec:
  replicas: 1

      - name: fetch-secrets

## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical CKAD debugging: handling slow-start upgrades with probes, init containers for bootstrapping state, and PD&B safeguards to prevent downtime during maintenance.

## Key Concepts

- startupProbe and readinessProbe tuning
- initContainer for pre-warming caches
- PodDisruptionBudget for upgrade safety
- RollingUpdate strategy and rollback procedures

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal patch sketch (Deployment snippet)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: invoice-processor
  namespace: payments
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: init-cache
        image: invoice-processor:2.1
        command: ["sh", "-c", "cp /config/* /var/cache/ || true"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config
          mountPath: /config
        - name: cache
          mountPath: /var/cache
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: invoice-processor:2.1
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 10
      volumes:
      - name: config
        secret:
          secretName: app-secret
      - name: cache
        emptyDir: {}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical CKAD skills including per-namespace configuration management, InitContainer usage, sidecar patterns, secure secret handling, and network policy implementation.

## Key Concepts
- Per-namespace deployments with shared persistent volumes
- InitContainer for runtime dependency installation
- Inotify-based file change detection and yamllint validation
- In-service reload capabilities (nginx -s reload)
- ConfigMap and Secret integration patterns
- TLS sidecar implementation for secure communications
- Namespace-level NetworkPolicy for egress restrictions

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton of the Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: config-watcher
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: config-watcher
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: config-watcher
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: install-tools
        image: alpine:latest
        command: ['sh', '-c', 'apk add --no-cache inotify-tools yamllint']
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:alpine
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-pvc
          mountPath: /config/dynamic
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
      - name: config-watcher
        image: alpine:latest
        command: ['sh', '-c', 'while inotifywait -e modify /config/dynamic/*.yaml; do yamllint /config/dynamic/*.yaml && nginx -s reload; done']
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-pvc
          mountPath: /config/dynamic
        env:
        - name: STATUS_URL
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: status-secret
              key: url
      - name: tls-sidecar
        image: envoyproxy/envoy:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
      volumes:
      - name: config-pvc
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: config-pvc
      - name: nginx-defaults
        configMap:
          name: nginx-defaults
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: config-pvc
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: nginx-defaults
  namespace: target-namespace
data:
  nginx.conf: |
    # Default Nginx configuration
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: status-secret
  namespace: target-namespace
type: Opaque
data:
  url: aHR0cDovL3N0YXR1cy5sb2NhbC9hcGkvdjEvcmVsb2Fk
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: config-watcher-netpol
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: config-watcher
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: internal-services
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
```

## Trade-offs
- **Inotify vs polling**: Inotify is more efficient but requires file system support
- **Sidecar overhead**: TLS sidecar adds complexity and resource usage
- **Single namespace scope**: Limited to namespace-level isolation vs cluster-wide
- **PVC dependency**: Requires storage management and backup strategies
- **Container sharing**: Process communication within pod vs separate services

Assesses practical CKAD skills: CronJob/Job TTL, InitContainers, ConfigMaps, PVCs, probes, RBAC, and NetworkPolicy with a realistic data-pruning task.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob and TTLAfterFinished
- InitContainer to stage scripts
- ConfigMap-driven parameters
- PVC mounting
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- RBAC least privilege via ServiceAccount
- NetworkPolicy egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: data-pruner
spec:
  schedule: "0 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: analytics-pruner
          initContainers:
          - name: stage-script
            image: busybox
            command: ["sh", "-c", "cp /scripts/prune.sh /prune.sh"]
          containers:
          - name: prune
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "/prune.sh"]
            resources:
              requests:
                memory: "64Mi"
                cpu: "100m"
              limits:
                memory: "128Mi"
                cpu: "250m"
            readinessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /healthz
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /healthz
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 20
          volumes:
          - name: data
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: dumps-pvc
          - name: scripts
            configMap:
              name: prune-scripts
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test TTLAfterFinished behavior in a staging cluster?
- What monitoring would you add for prune activity and failure retry logic?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical lifecycle management and how probes interact with rolling updates to avoid downtime.

## Key Concepts

- StartupProbe, readinessProbe, livenessProbe
- preStop and terminationGracePeriodSeconds
- Graceful shutdown patterns in Node.js apps

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-server
  namespace: prod
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web-server
        image: node:18
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        startupProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 3000
          failureThreshold: 30
          periodSeconds: 10
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 3000
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 3000
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 15
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["bash","-lc","sleep 5"]
        terminationMessagePath: /dev/termination-log
        terminationMessagePolicy: File
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "512Mi"
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you adjust thresholds for busy traffic?
- How would you verify graceful shutdown under load?
- What pitfalls exist with preStop sleeps in container runtimes?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD fundamentals: per-namespace scope, ConfigMaps, Secrets, InitContainers, and NetworkPolicy, plus practical image-signing workflow.

## Key Concepts
- PVC-mounted manifests and per-namespace scope
- InitContainer install and bootstrapping binaries (cosign)
- Batch processing using BATCH_SIZE from ConfigMap
- Secret-based API credentials and TLS sidecar rotation
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- NetworkPolicy restricting egress to internal signing endpoint

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton of image-signer Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: image-signer
  namespace: <ns>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: image-signer
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: image-signer
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: install-tools
        image: appropriate/curl
        command: ["sh", "-lc", "apk add --no-cache cosign jq; true"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: manifests
          mountPath: /manifests
      containers:
      - name: signer
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh", "-lc", "cron -f"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: manifests
          mountPath: /manifests
      volumes:
      - name: manifests
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: manifest-pvc
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test with dry-run and kubeval? 
- How would you handle large namespaces with many manifests?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests InitContainer sequencing, one-time data seeding, ConfigMap usage, and ensuring idempotent seeds and probes work with startup order.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainers run before app containers
- Seed data via idempotent SQL (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING)
- Mount seed script from ConfigMap
- Probes and resource requests/limits to keep health
- Validation under load and restart scenarios

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: inventory
  namespace: retail
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: seed-data
        image: postgres:15
        command: ["psql", "-h", "inventory-db", "-U", "seeduser", "-d", "inventory"]
        args: ["-f", "/seed/init.sql"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: seed-scripts
          mountPath: /seed
        env:
        - name: PGPASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: inventory-db-secret
              key: password
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: inventory-app:latest
        env:
        - name: DB_HOST
          value: "inventory-db"
        - name: DB_USER
          value: "seeduser"
        - name: DB_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: inventory-db-secret
              key: password
      volumes:
      - name: seed-scripts
        configMap:
          name: inventory-seed-scripts
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you avoid reseeding when pods are rescheduled and during upgrades?
- How would you test seed idempotency and monitor seed success during rolling updates?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills for multi-namespace automation, pod networking, and safe secret handling via Secrets and ConfigMaps.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob in a Namespace; PVC mounts
- InitContainer installation; jq usage
- Secret/ConfigMap usage; status tracking
- NetworkPolicy scoping; per-namespace egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: metrics-watcher
  namespace: <namespace>
spec:
  schedule: "*/5 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          containers:
          - name: collector
            image: registry.example/metrics-collector:latest
            volumeMounts:
            - name: metrics-pvc
              mountPath: /metrics
            - name: logs-pvc
              mountPath: /logs
            env:
            - name: ENDPOINT
              value: "https://metrics-portal:9090/api/v1/digest"
            - name: API_TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: metrics-secret
                  key: api-token
          initContainers:
          - name: install-tools
            image: appropriate/curl
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache jq && mkdir -p /logs"]
          volumes:
          - name: metrics-pvc
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: metrics-pvc
          - name: logs-pvc
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate the API token without restarting the CronJob?
- What are trade-offs of using a CronJob for real-time metrics vs. a DaemonSet collector?
